content: During the day, sunlight travels through a relatively thin layer of the atmosphere, allowing most of its blue wavelengths to scatter in all directions. However, as the sun approaches the horizon, its light must pass through a much thicker layer of air to reach your eyes. This increased path length causes the blue light to scatter away even more effectively, while the longer red wavelengths are less affected and continue to reach your eyes, making the sky appear red.
